evals.prompt: Our Go service has a single /health endpoint used for both the Kubernetes livenessProbe and readinessProbe, and it pings the database. When the database has a brief blip, all our pods restart at once instead of just being pulled from the load balancer. Why does this happen and how should we fix it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that conflating liveness and readiness in one endpoint means a database blip is treated as a liveness failure and triggers a restart storm, and recommends splitting into a liveness endpoint (process alive, no dependency checks) and a separate readiness endpoint (checks dependencies like the database).

assertions.text: Explains the restart-storm cause (liveness triggers restart, not just removal from rotation)
Recommends separate liveness and readiness endpoints

evals.prompt: We're planning a rolling deployment that both ships new application code and runs a migration that renames a column the old code still reads directly (not through the expand/migrate/contract pattern). Is a rolling deployment safe for this release?
evals.expected_output: Flags that a rolling deployment runs old and new code simultaneously against the same schema, so a non-backward-compatible schema change (a direct column rename) will break the old code instances still running during the rollout window, and recommends the expand/migrate/contract pattern instead.

assertions.text: Flags that old and new code run simultaneously during a rolling deploy
Recommends expand/migrate/contract or equivalent backward-compatible approach

evals.prompt: Our Go service currently starts up successfully even if the JWT_SECRET environment variable is missing, and only errors when the first request that needs it comes in, hours later, in production. What should we change about startup?
evals.expected_output: Recommends validating all required configuration (including JWT_SECRET) at process startup and exiting immediately with a non-zero status if anything required is missing, rather than starting successfully and failing later on first use.

assertions.text: Recommends failing fast / exiting rather than starting degraded
